The region above enclosed by the curves $y={x}^{2}+2$ and $y=20-{x}^{2}$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $y=20.$ Find the volume $V$ of the resulting solid. Do not round the answer.

$V=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we want to determine the limits of integration. We find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+2 & =20-{x}^{2} \\ 2{x}^{2} & =18 \\ {x}^{2} & =9 \\ x & =\pm 3\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, our limits of integration are from $x=-3$ to $x=3.$

Now, let's draw our vertical arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/f196ef4a3b29a9d62609b0a9290f34d2cb1ef1351baa4883441fd89e9345e4ed.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $y=20-{x}^{2},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $y={x}^{2}+2.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $y={x}^{2}+2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/c006e66d82e0059b341520bebe983fa75ed144e3050ca8c4493a4b6df3e8f352.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{-3}^{3}[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-3}^{3}[\,(20)-({x}^{2}+2)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-3}^{3}{[18-{x}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $y=20-{x}^{2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/c91a8e5ed0881ed0c8f34fa2ed6ccb5f95ff75a2f3b48e2d340f8a8856885e3a.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{-3}^{3}[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-3}^{3}[\,(20)-(20-{x}^{2})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-3}^{3}{[{x}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-3}^{3}{[18-{x}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x-\pi {\int }_{-3}^{3}{[{x}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-3}^{3}((18-{x}^{2})^{2}-({x}^{2})^{2})\,\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-3}^{3}(324-36{x}^{2}+{x}^{4}-{x}^{4})\,\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-3}^{3}(324-36{x}^{2})\,\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {(324x-12{x}^{3})|}_{-3}^{3} \\  & =\pi ((324(3)-12(3)^{3})-(324(-3)-12(-3)^{3})) \\  & =\pi ((972-324)-(-972+324)) \\  & =\pi (648-(-648)) \\  & =1296\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
